question: C3 as claimed: are the White House, the Saudi state and China's leadership aligned in a secret arrangement (level 2 or 3) while the public sees a march to war?

links.claim: On 10 March 2023 in Beijing, Saudi Arabia and Iran agreed, in a statement with China, to resume diplomatic relations and reopen embassies within two months. Signed for Saudi Arabia by National Security Adviser Musaad Al-Aiban, for Iran by Ali Shamkhani, for China by Wang Yi. Iran's embassy in Riyadh reopened 6 June 2023

actor.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

links.claim: In May 2025 the White House announced a 600 bn dollar Saudi investment commitment and a near 142 bn dollar arms sale (13 May), a 1.2 trillion dollar Qatar 'economic commitment' (14 May) and 200 bn dollars of UAE deals plus an accelerated 1.4 trillion dollar 10-year UAE framework (15 May). These are pledges, not completed flows

actor.name: The White House (Executive Office of the President)

links.claim: From 28 February 2026 the US and Israel struck Iran. Iran's IRGC announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz on 2 March. A two-week ceasefire was agreed 8 April. US Central Command began a naval blockade of Iranian ports on 13 April 2026 after talks in Islamabad failed

evidence.what: ABC News timeline of the 2026 Iran war, four phases

links.claim: China's foreign ministry said US and Israeli strikes were the 'root cause' of the Hormuz blockage, called the US blockade of Iranian ports 'irresponsible and dangerous' (April 2026) and in August 2026 urged the US and Iran to avoid a return to war

actor.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

evidence.what: Spokesman Guo Jiakun on the blockade
August statement by spokesman Lin Jian

links.claim: Each of the three (White House, Saudi state, China's State Council) has an interest in Hormuz reopening quickly and trade continuing (level 0)
footprints_expected: Public calls by each to reopen the strait
No party gains from a long closure in its own official accounts

footprints_found.what: China called for early restoration of free and safe passage
The US set a 48 hour ultimatum on 21 March to reopen the strait

footprints_missing: A Saudi official statement on the closure was not searched (budget)
rivals: The US blockade of Iranian ports shows the White House accepted a closed strait as a cost of pressure on Iran, so interests did not point the same way
China gained relative access when Iran let ships serving friendly countries pass, so its interest was not the same as the Gulf's
links.reveal: Saudi and US statements on Hormuz in the next escalation. Monthly China crude imports by origin (China customs, about the 20th of each month)

links.claim: The three run a level 2 secret arrangement in which the public conflict is staged or managed

actor.name: State Council of the People's Republic of China

footprints_expected: A named trilateral channel with dated meetings (a readout, a leak, a mirror account in Chinese or Gulf media)
An enforcement that stops one side cheating
Matched timing of moves by all three
No large real costs borne by any of the three
footprints_missing: No trilateral channel found in White House fact sheets, China foreign ministry statements or press searched this hole

Inconsistent marks found instead: China publicly condemned the US blockade. the strait was shut for months at real cost to China's oil imports. SAMA quietly left China's mBridge rail on 13 May 2025, the day of the US-Saudi package (see H4-03)
rivals: Level 0: overlapping interests on oil flow, with open rivalry on Iran and payment rails
Bilateral public deals (US-Gulf in May 2025, US-China in May 2026) that the public can read, so nothing is behind the scenes
links.reveal: Class L: declassification, memoirs, court records. No date. Near term: any readout of a US-Saudi-China meeting on Iran, or a leak of one

rival_hypotheses.text: Official: each state pursues its own stated aims. China brokered a Saudi-Iran deal for its own standing and oil security, the Gulf states bought US security and technology with investment pledges, and the US went to war with Iran over its nuclear programme
Coordination: the White House, the Saudi state and China's leadership agreed a shared plan in secret and the public conflict is staged or managed
Shared incentives: all three want Gulf oil to flow and trade to continue, so they often push the same way without a deal, and diverge where their interests split (Iran, payment rails)
Accident: the war and the Hormuz closure were escalations nobody planned, and the overlap of interests is coincidence of timing

coordination.channel: Claimed level 2. No trilateral channel found, so the level drops to 0
coordination.enforcement: None found. Nothing stops China or Saudi Arabia from defecting, and both took public positions against US moves (China on the blockade) or against China's rail (SAMA on mBridge)
coordination.secrecy_load: A staged war would need US Central Command, Israeli forces, Iran's IRGC and three governments' staff, thousands of people for over a year. Too heavy for the evidence
